title: Unified Access to the APSIMWISE Ecosystem
text: apsimwise collection interoperable R packages crop modelling, weather analysis, agricultural decision support. goal apsimwise provide consistent user-friendly interface APSIM-related workflows, allowing researchers, students, breeders, agronomists, consultants work multiple crops using common set tools.

text: package installs loads core apsimwise ecosystem, including: tidyweather weather data analysis. rapsimng manipulating APSIM Next Generation. rapsimng.wheat Wheat rapsimng.canola Canola rapsimng.chickpea Chickpea rapsimng.fababean Faba Bean rapsimng.lentil Lentil rapsimng.lupin Lupin additional crop packages become available

title: Unified Access to the APSIMWISE Ecosystem
text: apsimwise re-exports commonly used functions ecosystem users need load single package. complete list functions, see package documentation:
code: library(apsimwise)  # Read weather data met <- read_weather("weather.met")  # Calculate day length day_length(   date = met$date,   latitude = -27 )  # Calculate thermal time using crop-specific defaults thermal_time(   mint = met$mint,   maxt = met$maxt,   date = met$date,   latitude = -27,   crop = "lupin" )  # View crop-specific parameters crop("lupin")$get() help(package = "apsimwise")

title: Calculate thermal time for a crop — thermal_time
Calculate thermal time for a crop — thermal_time
code: library(apsimwise) # Example weather data mint <- c(0, 10) maxt <- c(30, 40) date <- as.Date(c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"))  # Use default lupin parameters thermal_time(   mint,   maxt,   date = date,   lat = -27,   crop = "lupin" ) #> [1] 16.64386 24.88400  # Modify the global lupin thermal time response for all following calculations crop("lupin")$set(   "phenology.thermal_time" =   list(     x = c(0, 25, 35),     y = c(0, 25, 0)   ) ) thermal_time(   mint,   maxt,   date = date,   lat = -27,   crop = "lupin" ) #> [1] 16.64386 24.88400  # Then the parameters can be reset crop("lupin")$reset()   # Override thermal time parameters for a single call thermal_time(   mint,   maxt,   date = date,   lat = -27,   crop = "lupin",   x_temp = c(0, 25, 35),   y_temp = c(0, 25, 0) ) #> [1] 16.64386 24.88400  # Calculate thermal time from a weather file met_file <- system.file("extdata/ppd_72150.met", package = "tidyweather") # Read weather records records <- read_weather(met_file) # Calculate thermal time for lupin using tidyverse ways library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: ‘dplyr’ #> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’: #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’: #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union records |>     mutate(         tt = thermal_time(             mint = mint,             maxt = maxt,             date = date,             latitude = latitude[1],             crop = "lupin"         )     ) |>     select(name, date, mint, maxt, tt) #> # A tibble: 587 × 5 #>    name            date        mint  maxt    tt #>    <chr>           <date>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #>  1 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-01  14.4  28.7  21.9 #>  2 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-02  15.1  29.1  21.5 #>  3 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-03  10    27.8  19.9 #>  4 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-04  14.6  30.4  22.8 #>  5 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-05  15.1  37.9  27.3 #>  6 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-06  18.5  33.3  25.6 #>  7 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-07  14.9  33.4  25.3 #>  8 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-08  20.4  36.4  29.0 #>  9 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-09  22.6  38.6  27.6 #> 10 WAGGA WAGGA AMO 2023-12-10  22.3  34.6  28.4 #> #
